newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Buthelezi calls for balanced view of South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Buthelezi calls for balanced view of South Africa.

text.p: Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) leader Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi on Friday called for a more balanced view of the role his party and the ruling African National Congress (ANC) played in South Africa's history.

"It takes two to tango, even in the tragic violence. Why are the atrocities of the ANC during that conflict overlooked?" said Buthelezi in response to criticism by anti-apartheid activists that his party was sympathetic to the country's former white regime.

In New Zealand to attend a meeting of Christians from around the world, Buthelezi -- who also is South Africa's home affairs minister -- said it was sheer temerity for people to criticise him in the name of the ANC.
"...I'm a minister of Mr Mandela's government. If I was not a Christian I would call it damn cheek," he said.
Anti-apartheid activist John Minto said Buthelezi was not welcome in New Zealand and must bear responsibility for some of the violence between Inkatha and ANC supporters in recent years.

"He (Buthelezi) shouldn't be here," Minto told Television New Zealand. "He was the right hand man of the white regime all the way through, giving them international credibility, and if he hadn't been there the apartheid system would have crumbled much quicker."
But Buthelezi called for a more equitable view.

"Why should they have disquiet about my visit? If there is a conflict between ANC and the IFP, why is there no disquiet about ANC leaders who come into this country, whose party was equally involved in the violence?" he asked.
"In fact, my party has lost more people and loses more people even now," he said.
Buthelezi was to attend the World Christian Gathering in Rotorua, in New Zealand's North Island, from November 10 to 17.
